damageClampWidth.question: Is 150 clamps against 7,194 refusals correct conservatism or an over-tight predicate?

damageClampWidth.reasoning: 6,231 refusals are no-material-damage — the node is not measurably damaged, so a clamp would be a guess dressed as a repair. The 363 containing-block-not-parent refusals on linear.app are damaged nodes refused correctly: the clamp's arithmetic is against the parent's content box and a grid item's containing block is its grid AREA. That is a MISSING MECHANISM, not an over-tight predicate.

costIncurred.mechanism: min-width: 0px is half of what grid-area-fill-width emits and is not optional — without it a grid item's automatic minimum size is its min-content width, which pushes the track wider than the recovered track list and puts the extent error straight back. With it the item box equals its track and any descendant still frozen at a truth-capture width spills INSIDE the box instead. The correction converts a right-extent error into an in-box overlap error.
